[FACT] User is concerned about the impact of social media on teenagers' mental health.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The rise of social media has affected teenagers' mental health in both positive and negative ways.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Social media has connected teenagers with like-minded individuals, providing a space for support, collaboration, and communication.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Research suggests that social media use is associated with depression, anxiety, and body image issues.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Social media creates pressure for teenagers to present themselves in a particular way, leading to comparison and self-criticism.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Exposure to cyberbullying and online hate can contribute to negative mental health outcomes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Parents and educators can promote a healthy relationship with social media by emphasizing balance and emotional regulation.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Strategies to address social media's impact include setting limits on screen time, monitoring social media use, and encouraging offline activities.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Teachers and mental health professionals can provide education, support, and resources for healthy coping mechanisms and self-esteem.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Social media platforms can take steps to prevent cyberbullying and foster a positive online community.  
[USER] Questions the responsibility of social media companies to regulate content and protect young users from harmful material.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Social media companies have a responsibility to regulate harmful content, but parents and educators also play an important role.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Social media companies have algorithms to flag harmful content, but these systems are not always foolproof.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Parents and educators can help teenagers identify harmful material and teach them how to report it.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Parents and educators can help teenagers develop healthy habits regarding social media use.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Protecting young users from harmful material is a joint effort between social media companies, parents, and educators.  
[USER] Asserts that social media companies should be held accountable for the negative impact their platforms have on teenagers' mental health.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Social media companies should be held accountable for their platforms' impact on teenagers' mental health.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Some companies have implemented features to limit screen time and filter harmful content.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] More needs to be done by social media companies to address mental health issues.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Companies should invest in research and develop solutions to mitigate negative effects.
